The Ethical Nucleus

The constellation

The next stage was the identification of a coherent ethical nucleus in the earliest
recoverable Jesus tradition. The principal components:

- *Post-Priestly Torah*
- *Q*
- *James*
- *Didache*

*A note on standing.* Two of these four are texts the project actually has — James and
the Didache are extant, read as themselves. The other two, Post-Priestly Torah and Q, are
scholarly reconstructions: a hypothesized redactional layer and a hypothesized document,
inferred rather than possessed. That distinction did not matter much while the
constellation was still being explored for its ethical content. It matters now — see
"Where this constellation stands now" at the end of this section.

These are not treated as interchangeable or identical. They are a constellation of
early ethical witnesses. Their common significance is the emergence of a way of life
centered on mercy, truth, righteousness, practical obedience, treatment of enemies,
generosity, integrity, non-retaliation, care for the vulnerable, purification of conduct,
and the transformation of ordinary human relationships.

The project therefore became concerned with *formation rather than belief alone*:

> What happens when the ethical teaching of Jesus is actually practiced as a way of life?

This is one of the decisive transitions into WMT.

The three witnesses

James

A vision of faith demonstrated through action. Its importance is the refusal to separate
spiritual authenticity from conduct. Wisdom must become behavior; faith must become
works. Speech, treatment of others, wealth, partiality, anger, judgment, and care for the
vulnerable all become tests of whether righteousness is actually present.

In the curriculum: the Moral Audit (`WMT PR01`) and Chapter Four, The Mirror
(`WMT C04`).

Q

A layer of Jesus tradition in which the kingdom is expressed through radical ethical
transformation — enemies, judgment, generosity, anxiety, possessions, retaliation, mercy,
and the Golden Rule. Q contributes substantially to the understanding of Jesus as teacher
of a radical way.

In the curriculum: Chapter Three, The Blueprint of Mercy (`WMT C03`), and
Non-Retaliation (`WMT PR06`).

Status: Q is a reconstruction, not an extant text — a hypothesis about a shared source
behind Matthew and Luke's common sayings material. It once functioned as part of the
ethical nucleus's foundation. It no longer does; see the closing note below.

Didache

Especially significant because it preserves an explicit ethical formation structure
through the *Two Ways* — the Way of Life and the Way of Death. This makes it central to
WMT's eventual emphasis on a path: Christianity is not merely something one believes,
it is something one walks.

In the curriculum: Chapter Five, The Apprenticeship (`WMT C05`), the Daily Anchors
(`WMT PR07`), and the Rule of Return (`WMT PR11`).

The early genealogy therefore already contains the basic architecture:

> truth → practice → character → way of life

A necessary clarification: this is not an anti-Pauline project

WMT should not be understood as a project against Paul. The central motivation was never
"defeat Paul." It was:

> "Recover the voices that became quieter."

James, Q, the Didache, and other early witnesses are allowed to speak in their own
voices. The project seeks to understand the historical development of Christianity by
recovering multiple early witnesses rather than allowing one later theological synthesis
to become the sole interpretive lens.

WMT is *recoverative and integrative, not polemical.* This distinction is essential and
should be preserved wherever the project is described.

Where this constellation stands now

For a time, this constellation — especially its reconstructive half, Post-Priestly Torah
and Q — functioned as the ethical nucleus's foundation: the ethics were secure because
they could be located in the earliest recoverable textual layer. That is no longer the
claim.

James and the Didache remain. They are texts the project actually has, not
reconstructions, and their content continues to inform the curriculum directly (`WMT
C04`, `WMT C05`, `WMT PR01`, `WMT PR07`, `WMT PR11`).

Post-Priestly Torah and Q were a stage the search passed through — an attempt to locate
an ethical core beneath the reconstructed textual history. That attempt shaped what came
after it, but it is not what the project's ethics currently rest on. What anchors WMT now
is the seven-stage developmental path (`WMT G06`, `WMT C25`) — a character-formation
architecture that stands on its own coherence, not on a contested reconstruction being
correct. Post-Priestly Torah and Q remain in this genealogy as an honest record of where
the search went, not as ongoing commitments.
